abilities.name: Attack
abilities.description: A measured strike with your weapon.
abilities._source: Convention: every class ships a free rank-1 Attack. It is also the hook ProcTrigger.ON_WEAPON_SWING fires off, which is what Zealotry listens for.

abilities.name: Righteous Lunge
abilities.description: Cover the ground between you and strike on the way in. Grants an Oath.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Open with Righteous Lunge to close the gap; it grants its own Oath', and 'Righteous Lunge is the only real engage'. Its Oath 'makes your abilities damage and heal for more'. The baseline builder for every spec.

abilities.name: Chastise
abilities.description: Call down a single hard blow of Holy force. Consumes two Oaths.
abilities._source: CoA: Chastise is the Oath Breaker all three specs share ('dump an Oath Breaker: Chastise, Blade of Faith, Divine Fury or Righteous Upheaval'). The cheap finisher, so it carries no cooldown - the Oath bank is its gate.

abilities.name: Condemn
abilities.description: Mark an enemy as condemned, burning them with Holy damage over 4 turns. Grants an Oath.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Condemn for the crit Oath and its stacking Holy damage-over-time', and 'Condemn carries a huge share of your damage per press'. Oathkeeper's Uther's Legacy and Crusader's Tyr's Blessing both key off it.

abilities.name: Holy Cleave
abilities.description: A wide sweep of Holy light that catches up to three enemies. Grants an Oath.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Build Holy Cleave for the extra-target Oath; around 10 stacks covers a normal pull'. Its Oath 'makes your abilities strike an additional nearby target', which has no engine hook, so the cleave is on the ability itself.

abilities.name: Temple Guardian
abilities.description: Charge to your allies' side. Everyone who sees you come is steadier for it.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Temple Guardian is your gap-closer and opener. It charges to an ally, healing you both, 3 charges on a 35 sec recharge'. There is no two-target heal and no charge system, so it heals the party on a short cooldown.

abilities.name: Benediction
abilities.description: Speak a blessing over a wounded ally. Consumes two Oaths.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Benediction is your baseline reactive heal. It scales with Stamina and consumes banked Oaths for extra healing'. The Stamina scaling is a real conversion key - see Oathkeeper's Fortified Body.

abilities.name: Blade of Faith
abilities.description: Drive your faith into the wound and leave it burning for 5 turns. Consumes three Oaths.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Blade of Faith, a long, hard-critting DoT' and 'Unleash a devastating Oath Breaker ... dealing AP Holy damage over 21 seconds'. Chained against Righteous Upheaval rather than spammed.

abilities.name: Divine Force
abilities.description: Leap at an enemy hard enough to put them on the ground and stop whatever they were saying.
abilities._source: CoA class tree: 'Leap at an enemy with divine force, stunning them for 6 seconds, dealing AP Holy damage, and interrupting non-player spellcasting'. The stun is real; the interrupt has no engine hook, and Interdict below carries the caster-shutdown half of the kit.

abilities.name: Interdict
abilities.description: Forbid an enemy from sinning. For 2 turns their spells will not find their mark.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Interdict silences a target and locks Undead and Demons out of healing'. No silence or cast-interrupt mechanic exists, so this follows the shipped Rogue Kick convention and guts the target's spell hit chance instead.

abilities.name: Silverhand Incantation
abilities.description: Throw a holy hammer and follow it in. It lands hard on everyone in front of you and mends everyone behind you. Consumes two Oaths.
abilities._source: CoA class tree: 'toss a holy hammer at your target, charging you to them ... you deal AP Holy damage to all nearby enemies and heal nearby allies for the same amount'. damage_and_heal with heal_scope party is exactly that shape.

abilities.name: Libram of Consecration
abilities.description: Read the consecration aloud. Everything you do for the next 3 turns lands with Holy force behind it, increasing your damage by 10%.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Libram of Consecration adds Holy damage to your damaging abilities' and 'Only one Libram can be active at a time'. damage_dealt_pct is the key a BUFF has to use - a buff's stat_mods never reach _damage_multiplier's talent lookups.

abilities.name: Libram of Fervor
abilities.description: Read the fervor aloud, and your training answers in a language it does not usually speak. Grants spell power equal to 30% of your Agility and attack power equal to 30% of your Intellect for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA class tree, verbatim: 'granting you spell power equal to 30% of your Agility and attack power equal to 30% of your Intellect for 20 seconds'. Both are real <target>_from_<source>_pct conversions, and the conversion loop in _recalculate_derived_stats reads the shared bonus pool, so a buff can carry them.

abilities.name: Libram of Zeal
abilities.description: Read the zeal aloud and stop pacing yourself. Increases your haste by 20 for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA Zealot: 'Libram of Zeal ... increasing your melee haste by 20%'.

abilities.name: Libram of Tenacity
abilities.description: Read the tenacity aloud. Physical blows land 20% lighter for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA class tree: 'reducing your Physical Damage taken by -30% for 20 seconds'. Trimmed to -20% because it sits on a 10 turn cooldown next to Guardian's Raise Shield (-40%, 2 turns) rather than being a panic button. NOTE the units: physical_damage_taken_pct is percentage POINTS in an ability's stat_mods and a FRACTION in a talent's effects.

abilities.name: Libram of Grace
abilities.description: Read the grace aloud. For 3 turns the light that follows you mends whoever is standing in it.
abilities._source: CoA: 'Libram of Grace makes each of them restore health to you and nearby allies, which on a large pull is party throughput'. The one Libram that is NOT in the exclusive group: the hot branch of _apply_effect does not pass exclusive_group to the StatusEffect it builds, so the one-Libram-at-a-time rule cannot bind a heal-over-time.

abilities.name: Testament of Fortitude
abilities.description: Stop fighting and meditate. Closes your wounds over 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA class tree: 'Meditate for 15 seconds, restoring 5% of your maximum health every 1 sec and reducing damage taken by -50%'. The mitigation half is dropped: a HOT's stat_mods never reach get_status_stat_mod, which is where damage_taken_pct is read, so it would have been silently inert. The heal is the half worth keeping.

abilities.name: Testament of Will
abilities.description: Break an ally free of whatever is holding them in place.
abilities._source: CoA class tree: 'Break an ally free of worldly constraints, making them immune to all movement impairing effects for 10 seconds'. No immunity window exists; a movement dispel is the honest half.

abilities.name: Testament of Faith
abilities.description: A prayer you only get to make once in a while, and it works.
abilities._source: CoA Oathkeeper weaknesses: 'Testament of Faith and the class kit's Libram of Tenacity each live on their own cooldown'. Its own class-tree node Final Prayer 'doubles the healing done to you by Testament of Fortitude and Testament of Faith', so it is a burst heal. Sacred Restraint cannot bind it - an instant heal leaves no StatusEffect for exclusive_group to sit on.

abilities.name: Testament of Hope
abilities.description: Two of you walk out of the light. Blows meant for you land 20% lighter for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA class tree: 'Summons 2 copies of yourself that charge at a nearby enemy and aid you in combat ... each copy reduces all damage you take by -10%'. summon_pet needs a template from combat/pet_templates.py and none of the fifteen is a mirror of the caster, so the copies are represented by the mitigation they grant: two copies, -10% each, -20%. damage_taken_pct is a FRACTION.

abilities.name: Vindication
abilities.description: A short, zealous strike that gets straight to the point. Grants an Oath.
abilities._source: CoA Zealot: 'Righteous Lunge and Vindication are your Oath builders, each granting an Oath, and Vindication triggers Zealotry'. Its own Oath gives 'your damaging abilities a 10% chance to trigger Zealotry'.

abilities.name: Righteous Upheaval
abilities.description: Bring everything you have been holding back down at once. Consumes three Oaths.
abilities._source: CoA Zealot: 'Unleash a dominating Oath Breaker, dealing SP Physical damage, increased by 3% for each time you triggered Zealotry during your Oath Chain'. Physical, not Holy, which is why it is the one Zealot finisher that does not want Holy scaling.

abilities.name: Divine Fury
abilities.description: A cleaving blow of Holy fire that comes apart on impact and catches up to four enemies. Consumes two Oaths.
abilities._source: CoA Zealot: 'Every ~10 Zealotries your Chastise becomes Divine Fury, a cleave holy hit that shreds armor'. There is no ability-transform mechanic, so it is its own button, and the armour shred is dropped - a damage ability cannot also apply a debuff.

abilities.name: Force of Golganneth
abilities.description: Detonate. The light keeps going off for 3 turns and everything nearby stays inside it.
abilities._source: CoA Zealot: 'Force of Golganneth is a two-minute cooldown that explodes for holy damage and triggers Zealotry on every nearby enemy for several seconds' and 'Force of Golganneth is your best AoE button'. A repeating explosion over several seconds is a DoT here.

abilities.name: Mortal Abdication
abilities.description: One strike, delivered like a verdict.
abilities._source: CoA names Mortal Abdication twice as a Zealot cooldown (One With The Light 'reduces the cooldown of Librams, Force of Golganneth, and Mortal Abdication', and Libram of Zeal is read 'from your Libram of Mortal Abdication') without ever stating what it does. Implemented as the single-target counterpart to Force of Golganneth on the same cooldown band, which is the only thing the surrounding text supports. GAP: its real mechanic is not in the reference.

abilities.name: Norgannon's Wrath
abilities.description: Leap, hang a moment, and come down as a column of light. Consumes two Oaths.
abilities._source: CoA Zealot tier-6 talent, verbatim: 'Target an enemy and leap into the air. After a short delay, you blast them with immense holy force, dealing holy AP Holy damage to up to 10 enemies within 5 yds'. A talent in CoA, so a talent here: unlocked by the Zealot capstone, hence requires_talent. The immunity-piercing and the damage/healing-done debuff have no engine hooks.

abilities.name: Sacred Swing
abilities.description: Swing wide at everything in front of you. Grants an Oath.
abilities._source: CoA Oathkeeper: 'Sacred Swing (usable off an avoided attack)' and 'Use Sacred Swing on cooldown whenever it's up, after a dodge or parry, for cheap AoE damage and a Staffguard absorb'. The dodge/parry gate has no engine hook - no ability can require a recent avoidance - so it sits on a 2 turn cooldown instead, which is the closest honest throttle. Staffguard is the talent that reads it.

abilities.name: Reckoning
abilities.description: Call the whole pull to account at once, striking up to four enemies. Consumes two Oaths.
abilities._source: CoA Oathkeeper: 'Spend into Reckoning as your default Oath Breaker while leveling. It deals AoE Holy damage and restores Energy per enemy struck'. The Energy refund is dropped - a finisher that refunded Combo would undo its own cost, and the Templar has no second pool to refund into. Sacred Resistance is the talent that reads it.

abilities.name: Absolution
abilities.description: Make yourself the only thing in the room worth hitting.
abilities._source: CoA Oathkeeper: 'Taunt all enemies within 8 yds for 4 seconds', 'Pull with Absolution to taunt and establish threat' and 'Use Absolution to peel adds off the actual healer'. Implemented as a threat_generation_pct buff, the convention Guardian's Challenging Cry (200) and Cultist's Twilight Domain (180) already use - an ability buff's stat_mods are percentage POINTS here, unlike a talent's effects, which are fractions.

abilities.name: Barrier of Light
abilities.description: Put a wall of light around your allies. Healing reaches them 30% better through it.
abilities._source: CoA Oathkeeper: 'Emit saving light, increasing the healing received by nearby allies by 40% for 15 seconds. For the duration, threat generated by your allies is redirected to you.' The redirect half is dropped: one stat_mods dict applies to every recipient, so a threat key here would land on the allies too, which is backwards.

abilities.name: Spiritual Abdication
abilities.description: Set your own body aside for 3 turns. What is left standing is harder to hurt.
abilities._source: CoA Oathkeeper's Spiritual Abdicator node ('Your Spiritual Abdication now reduces damage taken by an additional -5% per copy') is the only mention of the ability, and it names copies and damage reduction, so this is Testament of Hope's defensive sibling. GAP: the ability's own tooltip is not in the reference.

abilities.name: Tome of Light
abilities.description: Open the tome. For 3 turns a shield of light takes the hits instead of you.
abilities._source: CoA Oathkeeper: 'Tome of Light shields for 100% of max health', 'Pop Tome of Light's full-health shield as your defensive cooldown when a burst AoE phase hits'. A tier-6 talent in CoA, so a talent here. 100% of max health is far outside what any shipped absorb does (Cultist's Eldritch Bastion, the biggest, is 0.35), so it lands at 0.40 - the largest in the game, without being triple the next one.

abilities.name: Argent Blade
abilities.description: A blow struck with argent fervour. What it takes out of them comes back into you. Grants an Oath.
abilities._source: CoA Crusader: 'Crush an enemy with argent fervor ... healing you equal to the damage dealt, and extending the duration of your Oath Chain by 3 sec', 'keep Argent Blade flowing to extend the Oath Chain'. There is no Oath Chain timer, so extending it becomes generating an Oath, which is the same thing: the Combo bank IS the Chain. The heal goes through heal_scope lowest_ally, so solo it lands on the Templar as written, and in a party it finds whoever needs it more.

abilities.name: Titanstrike
abilities.description: Finish a wounded enemy and take back what the fight cost you. Consumes two Oaths.
abilities._source: CoA Crusader: 'Titanstrike is your execute below 35% health and heals you for the damage dealt, twice that with Titanfall talented'. execute_threshold_pct is a PERCENT here, not a fraction - the engine compares it against target health on a 0-100 scale, and every shipped execute (Warrior 20, Cultist 35, Primalist 25/50) is written that way.

abilities.name: Righteous Tempest
abilities.description: Open up and keep turning for 3 turns. Consumes four Oaths, the whole bank.
abilities._source: CoA Crusader: 'Unleash a whirling Oath Breaker, dealing Weapon Damage plus SP damage to nearby enemies ... every 1 sec for 3 seconds' and 'Righteous Tempest consumes the entire bank for a 3-second whirl'. The only 80-cost ability in the kit, which is the whole 100 pool minus one Oath. A talent in CoA, so requires_talent here.

abilities.name: Scarlet Hammer
abilities.description: Drop a scarlet hammer on them from somewhere above.
abilities._source: CoA Crusader: 'Drop a scarlet hammer on an enemy for 155% Weapon Damage plus 35 as Holy Damage and reduce their Armor by 555 for 10 seconds'. Reached in CoA by casting Argent Blade under Warrior of Dawn, which no ability-transform mechanic can express, so it is its own button. The armour reduction is dropped for the same reason as Divine Fury's.

abilities.name: Crusader's Brand
abilities.description: Brand an enemy. They are not getting away from you, and they will feel it every time they swing.
abilities._source: CoA Crusader: 'Crusader's Brand pins a runner so they cannot flee, mount, or speed away, and reveals them through stealth'. No movement, mount or stealth systems exist, so the pin is a haste slow, the shipped convention for a snare (Rogue's Crippling Poison, -30).

abilities.name: Divine Charge
abilities.description: You and yours come up onto the light and move. Increases the party's haste by 15 for 3 turns.
abilities._source: CoA Crusader: 'Divine Charge gives the party a mounted speed burst outdoors that does not break on casting', 'Divine Charge only works outdoors, so it is not your dungeon opener'. There is no indoor/outdoor gate and no movement speed, so it is a party haste window. The trample damage is dropped.

abilities.name: Testament of Strength
abilities.description: Swear the strength oath. For 3 turns Titanstrike needs no wounded enemy, and everything you do hits 25% harder.
abilities._source: CoA Crusader tier-6: 'Your next 3 Titanstrikes are usable regardless of your target's health percentage and deal 25% increased damage. Lasts 1 minute.' The HP-gate bypass is real, not an approximation: a buff carrying proc.bypass_execute_threshold is exactly what use() checks before the execute gate (the hook Warrior's Sudden Death was written for). One use per cast, since use() strips the effect when it spends it.
